turns.t: Hi, quickly please, I'm on my lunch break. I slipped on ice this morning on the way to the car and landed on my left hand. My wrist is killing me.
Thanks for coming straight in. Describe the pain.
Sharp, right at the base of the thumb side, worse if I try to turn the hand over.
Can you move your fingers? ~
Yes, I can wiggle them. ~
Any numbness or tingling?
No. None.
Any other medical conditions I should know about?
Just asthma.
Let me take your numbers. Pulse 82, blood pressure 124 over 80, temperature 36.7, oxygen 99 percent, breathing 16.
Is that okay? ~
Fine. Now, I want to explain what I'm thinking. When someone falls onto an outstretched hand, one of the small bones in the wrist, or the end of the forearm bone, can crack. ~
Is it broken? ~
I can't say without an X-ray. But with this kind of fall and pain on the thumb side, I think it's possibly a fracture of the wrist.
Great. I've got a presentation tomorrow. ~
I understand. The X-ray will answer the question quickly. I'd like to arrange an X-ray of the wrist, today.
Where? ~
Radiology is down the corridor. They'll fit you in. ~
Fine. And in the meantime? ~
Keep it elevated on a pillow, and use a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for twenty minutes at a time.
Okay. ~
Don't use the hand to lift anything. A sling would help for a few hours.
I'll ask the nurse. ~
For the pain, you can take paracetamol, nothing more than the label says. ~
Right. ~
Take the X-ray result back to the front desk, and they'll find me. ~
Will you look at it today? ~
Yes. If the X-ray shows a fracture, I'll refer you to the fracture clinic right away for a cast.
Okay. And if it doesn't? ~
Then we'll treat it as a sprain, with a wrist splint. ~
That I can handle. ~
Good luck with the presentation. ~
Thanks. I'll need it. ~
